title: Vet Nurse Salary Australia: How to Calculate Annual Pay from Your Hourly Rate

faqs.q: What is the current minimum hourly rate for a veterinary nurse in Australia?
faqs.a: Under the Animal Care and Veterinary Services Award 2020, from 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rates are: Introductory level $25.74, Level 1 $26.44, Level 2 $28.24, Level 3 $29.45, and Level 4 $32.13. These rates apply to full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate as a vet nurse?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, a Level 2 vet nurse at $28.24 per hour: $28.24 × 38 × 52 = $55,788.24 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Superannuation is paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: Does the vet nurse salary include superannuation?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Vet Nurse Pay in Australia

If you're searching for "vet nurse salary australia", you're likely trying to figure out how your hourly rate translates into an annual figure. Whether you're a veterinary nurse, a practice manager, or a receptionist in the animal care industry, your pay is governed by the **Animal Care and Veterinary Services Award 2020**. This award sets minimum wages, penalty rates, and conditions for employees in veterinary practices.

This guide walks you through the standard calculation: hourly rate × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks. We'll also cover fortnightly pay, casual loading, superannuation, and tax – all using the latest figures from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office.

## How Vet Nurse Pay Is Set

The award classifies veterinary nurses and other staff into levels based on experience and responsibility. For full-time and part-time employees, the minimum hourly rates from 1 July 2026 are:

- **Introductory level**: $25.74 per hour
- **Level 1**: $26.44 per hour
- **Level 2**: $28.24 per hour
- **Level 3**: $29.45 per hour
- **Level 4**: $32.13 per hour
- **Practice manager (Level 5)**: $33.77 per hour

These rates come from the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guide. The award also covers veterinary surgeons (vets) with higher rates, but this article focuses on vet nurses and support staff.

## From Hourly to Annual: The 38-Hour Week

The standard full-time week under the award is 38 ordinary hours. To convert your hourly rate to an annual salary, use this formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, a **Level 2 veterinary nurse** earning $28.24 per hour:

$28.24 × 38 = $1,073.12 per week
$1,073.12 × 52 = **$55,802.24 per year** (rounded to $55,802)

This matches the award's weekly rate of $1,073.10 (minor rounding difference). You can use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to check other rates.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Simply multiply the weekly amount by 2:

$1,073.12 × 2 = **$2,146.24 per fortnight**

This is useful for budgeting and comparing with job advertisements that quote fortnightly figures.

## Casual Loading and Annual Pay

Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate, instead of paid leave entitlements. For a casual Level 2 vet nurse:

$28.24 × 1.25 = $35.30 per hour

Annual equivalent (if working 38 hours every week):
$35.30 × 38 × 52 = **$69,752.80 per year**

Remember, casuals don't get paid annual leave or sick leave, so the higher rate compensates for that. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must contribute superannuation at 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). This is **on top of** your base salary. For a full-time Level 2 vet nurse earning $55,802:

Super contribution = $55,802 × 0.12 = **$6,696 per year**

Super is paid into a fund of your choice, such as AustralianSuper, and is not part of your take-home pay. The maximum earnings subject to super is $270,830 per year (2026–27). See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for details.

## Tax on Your Vet Nurse Salary

Income tax in 2026–27 uses these resident rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- Over $190,000: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners).

For a Level 2 vet nurse earning $55,802:

- Taxable income: $55,802
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 0.15 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $55,802: ($55,802 – $45,000) × 0.30 = $3,240.60
- Total tax: $4,020 + $3,240.60 = **$7,260.60**
- Medicare levy (2%): $55,802 × 0.02 = $1,116.04
- Total tax + Medicare: **$8,376.64**

Take-home pay: $55,802 – $8,377 = **$47,425 per year** (approximately $912 per week).

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

## Comparing with National Minimum Wage and Averages

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. A Level 1 vet nurse earns exactly that rate. Higher levels pay above the minimum.

According to the **Australian Bureau of Statistics** (Average Weekly Earnings, May 2026), full-time adult ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70 per week. A Level 4 vet nurse at $32.13 per hour earns $1,221 per week – below the national average, reflecting the award's role in setting minimums for this industry.

## Important Notes

- This calculation assumes you work exactly 38 hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances.
- Award rates change each 1 July. Always check the latest [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses 2025–26 reduction thresholds (not confirmed for 2026–27).
- HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included.

## Conclusion

When researching "vet nurse salary australia", remember that your annual pay depends on your award classification, hours, and whether you're casual. The standard method – hourly rate × 38 × 52 – gives a reliable gross figure. Add super on top, subtract tax and Medicare for take-home pay. For a quick estimate, try our [the timesheet](/), which lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

Always refer to the [reference tables](/data) for the latest award rates, and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman if you're unsure about your classification.
